sections.content: How many people are "elected officers and representatives"?

6,810 people

were counted on the census as "elected officers and representatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Elected representatives in national government formulate and ratify legislation and government policy, act as elected representatives in Parliament, Regional Parliaments or Assemblies, and as representatives of the government and its executive.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "elected officers and representatives" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 65 years or older. Of the whole working population 4.2% were aged 65 years or older. For people working as "elected officers and representatives", 37.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "elected officers and representatives" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "elected officers and representatives" included:

  • farmers
  • managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture
  • exam invigilators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "elected officers and representatives" there were more men than women (57.6% compared with 42.4%).

This means "elected officers and representatives" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 57.6% and women made up 42.4% of "elected officers and representatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "elected officers and representatives" included:

  • sports and leisure assistants
  • ambulance staff (excluding paramedics)
  • quality assurance technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "elected officers and representatives", 19.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (50.4% compared with 49.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (85.6%) than self-employed (14.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
